read_only.title: Read-only mode
read_only.description: Read-only mode applies to every device on this account. Home Assistant keeps the camera stream, sensors and motion and sound detection, but gets no control over device settings: camera power or sleep, night light, volume and Sound & Light controls are removed, and automations that use them stop working. Turning it off brings them back with the same names and entity IDs.

local_stream.title: Local streaming
local_stream.description: With local streaming on, the camera sends its video straight to Home Assistant over your network instead of through the Nanit cloud, encrypted with a certificate Home Assistant creates. The camera must be able to reach Home Assistant on the port below. If it can't, the integration falls back to the cloud stream and tells you why.

data_description.local_stream_port: TCP port Home Assistant listens on for the camera. If it is taken, the next few ports are tried, unless an advertised address is set.
data_description.local_stream_host: Leave blank to detect it. Set it when Home Assistant runs in a container with bridge networking (use the host's LAN address and publish the port), or when Home Assistant has more than one network connection and the camera is on one that isn't the default (use Home Assistant's address on the camera's network).

stream_stills.title: Stills from the live stream
stream_stills.description: Fills the camera's picture (HomeKit tiles, picture cards) from the live stream when Nanit's cloud has no still, as it currently has none. When a picture is asked for and the last one is more than about 10 minutes old, Home Assistant starts the camera's stream briefly and keeps one frame. The camera then keeps streaming for about 20 minutes and holds one of its stream slots (it allows about two), so an always-visible tile keeps it streaming and leaves one fewer phone able to watch live. Nothing is taken while the camera is asleep. Needs FFmpeg, which Home Assistant OS and Container include. Applies to every camera on this account, and changing it reloads the integration.

init.title: Nanit camera can't reach Home Assistant for local streaming
init.description:
Using the Nanit cloud stream instead. The camera was told to send its video to `{address}` but never connected, twice in a row. Allow TCP port {port} to Home Assistant in the host firewall, and publish the port if Home Assistant runs in a container. If the camera is on another network or VLAN, allow it to reach Home Assistant on that port in your router. If Home Assistant has its own address on the camera's network, set that as the advertised address in the Nanit integration options.

Local streaming is paused and is retried automatically every 24 hours. Submit this repair once you've fixed it to retry right away.

local_stream_unreachable_docker.title: Nanit camera can't reach Home Assistant for local streaming

init.title: Nanit camera can't reach Home Assistant for local streaming
init.description:
Using the Nanit cloud stream instead. The camera was told to send its video to `{address}` but never connected, twice in a row. Home Assistant looks like it runs in a container with bridge networking, so publish the port (`-p {port}:{port}`) or use host networking, and set the advertised address to the host's LAN IP in the Nanit integration options.

Local streaming is paused and is retried automatically every 24 hours. Submit this repair once you've fixed it to retry right away.

init.title: Nanit local streaming keeps failing
init.description: Using the Nanit cloud stream instead. The camera reached Home Assistant at `{address}` but the connection kept failing, so local streaming is paused and retried every 24 hours. This is probably a bug: please open an issue with a debug log from the Nanit integration.
